source_snapshot.items: Test connections between BMC I2C-5, RTC and IO expander
source_snapshot.procedure: On BMC run `i2cdetect -y -q 4` and forced `i2ctransfer -f -y 4 w1@0x6f 0x0b r1`; consult PID1114953.
source_snapshot.criteria: Only generic evidence/photo and unexpected-log checks; no bus mapping,0x6f device identity, register value or separate IO-expander oracle.
source_snapshot.deepseek: NO; replaces an explicit remote transaction with unsupported probing/soldering.
source_snapshot.gpt_v2: MANUAL ONLY/CHANGED; identifies logical-I2C-versus-Linux-bus and `-f` risks, but still invents physical acceptance and does not show how one byte covers RTC plus IO expander.

Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.). Log into the BMC and run the following command and ensure you get a reply. Refer to PID : 1114953 for other devices expected on the bus. i2cdetect -y -q 4 i2ctransfer -f -y 4 w1@0x6f 0x0b r1""

test_case.test_name: Test connections between BMC I2C-5, RTC and IO expander — retained controlled review-layer procedure
test_case.purpose: Verify BMC I2C-5 can communicate with the RTC and IO expander while preserving system timekeeping and IO state, with separate evidence for each named endpoint.
required_package: PID1114953 mapping from BMC I2C-5 to Linux bus4 and both RTC/IO-expander endpoints
Device identity at0x6f and authoritative meaning/access mode of register0x0b
Separate IO-expander address, safe identity/input-status register and expected value/mask if0x6f is the RTC
RTC expected format, clock source, reference/tolerance and read consistency/progression rules
Kernel RTC and GPIO/IO-expander driver ownership plus approved sysfs/driver interface or raw-access exception
Timeout/NACK/error criteria, clock/GPIO preservation and recovery
test_case.test_command: Prove logical BMC I2C-5 maps to Linux bus4; identify RTC and IO-expander addresses from PID1114953; inspect kernel/daemon ownership; read safe identity/status/time registers through the supported driver or approved raw path; validate RTC time progresses against a reference and IO-expander state matches the non-mutating oracle; avoid broad scans and forced access where possible; confirm no clock/GPIO changes.
test_case.expected_result: 【After Test】 1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders. 2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test."

Define RTC time format/reference/tolerance, kernel driver ownership and whether `-f` is permitted, safe scan policy, timeout/NACK criteria, clock/GPIO preservation and recovery; confirm physical probing is not mandatory unless separately scoped.
safety_gate: Prefer kernel/driver read interfaces; do not use `-f` while a bound driver owns0x6f absent explicit platform approval
Do not scan arbitrary bus4 addresses with quick-write discovery
Confirm register0x0b is read-safe and no pointer/read side effect clears flags or latches
Do not set time, alarms or IO directions/outputs; capture clock and GPIO state before/after
Abort on time jump, driver error, unexpected IO change, NACK, timeout, stuck bus or BMC degradation
expected_evidence: PID map for BMC I2C-5/bus4 and both RTC/IO-expander endpoints
BMC identity, RTC/IO device IDs, kernel driver bindings and access-owner baseline
Vendor definitions for0x6f register0x0b and separate IO-expander safe register
Timestamped RTC raw/decoded values across an interval versus reference with tolerance
Timestamped IO-expander expected-versus-observed status/value without direction/output change
Pre/post clock, alarms, GPIO, bus/BMC health and engineer verdict
test_case.recovery: Wistron I2C policy requires BMC controller/bus, every target address, expected response and recovery. Kernel ownership is especially relevant for the RTC and IO-expander GPIO state.
